title: NRLW Salary Cap and Your Pay: How to Convert Hourly Rates to Annual, Fortnightly, and More
description: Understand the NRLW salary cap in context of Australian pay standards. Learn to convert hourly rates to annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay using 38-hour weeks and 52-week years.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week over 52 weeks, annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 1976 hours.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then multiply by 52. For a standard 38-hour week, that's hourly × 1976. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. It is paid on top of the minimum wage or award rate. For example, the national minimum wage of $26.44 per hour becomes $33.05 per hour for casual employees.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in my hourly rate or paid on top?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026). It is not part of your hourly rate; your employer must contribute it separately up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year.

## From Hourly Rate to Annual Pay: The 38-Hour Week, Fortnight, and 52-Week Year

Whether you are comparing a job offer, budgeting, or just curious, understanding how your hourly rate translates into annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay is essential. In Australia, most full-time employees work a 38-hour week, and the standard year is 52 weeks. This article explains the conversion, the role of the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, and superannuation – and touches on how the NRLW salary cap fits into the broader pay landscape.

### The Basic Formula

The core calculation is straightforward: annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For a 38-hour week, that is hourly rate × 1976. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, annual pay is $26.44 × 1976 = $52,245.44 before tax. If you work a different number of hours per week, adjust accordingly. The same formula works for fortnightly pay: hourly rate × hours per week × 2. So a fortnight at 38 hours per week is 76 hours, giving $26.44 × 76 = $2,009.44.

### The National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the legal floor for award-free employees. However, most workers are covered by a modern award or enterprise agreement that sets higher minimum rates for their industry or role. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award. Always check your award first – the National Minimum Wage is only a safety net.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For the National Minimum Wage, that means $33.05 per hour. When using our [timesheet](/), you can check a box to add casual loading automatically. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading – the tool adds it for you.

### Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your gross pay. It is not deducted from your hourly rate. For 2026–27, the maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year. So if your annual pay exceeds that, super only applies up to that cap. For most workers, super adds a significant boost to your total remuneration.

### Tax and Medicare

Your take-home pay depends on tax. The 2026–27 resident tax rates are: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on earnings up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. These are deducted from your gross pay. The calculator on this site uses these rates with the full tax-free threshold.

### The NRLW Salary Cap in Context

The NRLW salary cap sets a maximum total player payments for women's rugby league teams. While that cap is a specific figure negotiated between the league and the players' union, it illustrates how different industries set pay ceilings. For most Australian workers, pay is determined by awards, agreements, or the National Minimum Wage – not a cap. The NRLW salary cap is a useful reminder that pay structures vary widely, but the hourly-to-annual conversion remains the same.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by two. For a 38-hour week at the National Minimum Wage, that is $2,009.44. If you are casual, it is $2,511.80. This is handy for budgeting.

### Important Assumptions

This conversion assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more detail on minimum rates, see our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page. To understand casual loading better, visit [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading).
